title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the notational preliminaries of the 1976 IHÉS lecture notes on the divided-power de Rham complex. On the previous page Grothendieck fixed conventions for simplicial objects, written with lower indices: A_* = Hom(Δ°, A), K_* = (K_{[n]}). Cosimplicial objects get upper indices: A^* = Hom(Δ, A), K^* = (K^{[n]}). A bicosimplicial-simplicial object K^*_* ∈ (A_*)^* ≃ Hom(Δ×Δ°, A) then has components K^{[m]}_{[n]} = K(Δ^m, Δ^n).

This page extends the convention to the other three mixed-variance double objects:
- K_*^* ∈ (A^*)_* ≃ Hom(Δ°×Δ, A);
- K^{**} ∈ (A^*)^*, which should be Hom(Δ×Δ, A);
- K_{**} ∈ A_{**} ≃ Hom(Δ°×Δ°, A).

He then warns about a notational ambiguity. Precomposing with the swap of factors (inside Δ×Δ or Δ°×Δ°, or between Δ×Δ° and Δ°×Δ) is not recorded by the index notation. Under the 'raising and lowering of indices' convention, the transform of K^*_* would be written K_*^*, and that of K^{**} would again be K^{**}, giving the absurd-looking identity K^{[m][n]} = K^{[m][n]}. So he introduces an explicit symmetry symbol σ, writing the swapped object as ^σK.

He illustrates with a partial evaluation. Given K^*_*, fix n and set K^*_{[n]} := ([m] ↦ K^{[m]}_{[n]}), a cosimplicial object (∈ A^*). The functor [n] ↦ K^*_{[n]} is then an object of (A^*)_*, and it is exactly ^σK (currying in the other variable). He announces the same conventions for symbols with more than two indices, i.e. iterated categories like (((A^*)_*)^*)^*.

Purpose: bookkeeping for the multisimplicial/cosimplicial constructions to come. The next page turns to the universal cosimplicial object Δ^* and the equivalence A^* ≃ colimit-preserving functors Ss → A (Kan extension / nerve–realization). These serve the construction of the divided-power de Rham complex via cosimplicial and Dold–Kan methods.
errors: The identification (A^*)^* ≃ Hom(Δ°×Δ, A) for K^{**} appears to be a slip (copied from the previous line). By the stated conventions (A^* = Hom(Δ, A)) it should be Hom(Δ×Δ, A).
The marginal annotation '∈ Ob(A^*)^*_*' is garbled; the intended category for the curried object [n] ↦ K^*_{[n]} is (A^*)_*. This is a minor notational slip.

ideas.what: Index-position notation for simplicial (lower) versus cosimplicial (upper) variance, extended to bi- and multi-(co)simplicial objects, with currying equivalences (A_*)^* ≃ Hom(Δ×Δ°, A) etc.
ideas.modern_name: bisimplicial/bicosimplicial objects; currying of functor categories; Einstein-style variance notation
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard folklore (Bousfield–Kan, Quillen, Illusie for multisimplicial conventions)
ideas.where_published: Similar variance conventions appear in Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs in spirit, but not this exact text

ideas.what: Explicit symmetry operator σ swapping the two simplicial directions, and its identification with currying in the other variable.

deep.surprise_reason: Purely notational conventions for bisimplicial/bicosimplicial objects and their transposes; standard material with no new mathematics, though historically it documents Grothendieck's careful variance bookkeeping in the 1976 lecture.
transcription_corrections: 'la convention plus haut de la "mutation et discarder des indices"' should almost certainly read 'la convention plus haut de la "montée et descente des indices"' (raising and lowering of indices).
Line 3: the image reads (A^*)^* ≃ Hom(Δ°×Δ, A), apparently Grothendieck's own slip for Hom(Δ×Δ, A); it is not a transcription error.
Marginal annotation near ^σK: likely intended as '∈ Ob(A^*)_*'.
